The quoted passage is at p.10 under '3. Examples: [akat] with H-H tone 'tongue', [akat] with L-L tone 'food'; [mua] with H-L tone 'l…
new_statements.relation_note: Two level tones (H, L) and a falling tone, tentative analysis, with a tonal minimal pair; no stress statement.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ngaalam is analysed (tentatively) as a tone language with two level tones, High and Low, plus a falling (HL) contour; tone is lexically contrastive (minimal pair akat H-H 'tongue' vs akat L-L 'food'). Nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the author flags the tone analysis as tentative
new_statements.identity_note: First-hand: the author (Addis Ababa University phonetician who identified the group in January 2015) gives Language Name Ngaalam, Nilo-Saharan > East Sudanic > Surmic (South West Surmic pattern), location Gambella Regional State, Anuak Zone, Dima District, Koy locality, self-name also Tama [t'ama], population ~1500 -- exactly Glottolog's ngaa1241 (Ngalam/Olam), not Baale/Kacipo-Balesi (kaci1244). The linguistic data are stated to come from the author's own 2015 handout 'Ngaalam: sketch of grammar and its genetic position'.
